title: Keyboard Accessibility
content: All functionality of the content must be operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes, except where the underlying function requires input that depends on the path of the user's movement and not just the endpoints.
recommended_alternatives: Ensure standard focusable button or anchor elements with keyboard Enter/Space activation
Provide keyboard shortcuts and sequential Tab navigation
Expose actionable controls to the accessibility tree via semantic elements

title: Focus Visible
content: Any keyboard operable user interface must have a mode of operation where the keyboard focus indicator is visible. When focus moves to an element, users must be able to visually track which control has active focus.
recommended_alternatives: Maintain a clear high-contrast focus ring (min 3:1 contrast ratio)
Programmatically move focus into opened dialogs/modals and return focus on close
Ensure active document.activeElement is visibly styled

title: Dragging Movements
content: All functionality that uses a dragging movement for operation can be achieved by a single pointer without dragging, unless dragging is essential. Dragging actions, such as drag-and-drop file upload, item reordering, and slider repositioning, present severe barriers for users with tremors, motor impairments, head pointers, or screen readers.
recommended_alternatives: Provide 'Move Up' and 'Move Down' buttons or numeric position selectors
Provide standard 'Browse Files' file picker input button alongside drag zones
Add context menu or action buttons (e.g. 'Select Destination' or keyboard reorder)

title: Target Size (Minimum)
content: The size of the target for pointer inputs must be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except where spacing is sufficient or an inline link in a sentence. Tiny targets lead to accidental touches and extreme difficulty for users with tremors or physical disabilities.
recommended_alternatives: Ensure interactive elements meet minimum 24x24px (preferably 44x44px) bounding box
Add surrounding padding to click targets to expand hit area
Provide generous spacing between adjacent touch targets

title: Labels or Instructions
content: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input. Users who are blind or have cognitive limitations need clear visible and programmatic labels explaining what format or data is expected.
recommended_alternatives: Explicitly associate <label for='...'> with input elements
Provide persistent instructional hints above or below inputs
State required constraints (e.g. date format, file extensions) upfront

title: Name, Role, Value
content: For all user interface components (including form elements, links, and components generated by scripts), the name and role can be programmatically determined; states, properties, and values that can be set by the user can be programmatically set; and notification of changes to these items is available to user agents, including assistive technologies.
recommended_alternatives: Use semantic HTML elements (<button>, <select>, <nav>, <main>)
Set proper aria-label, aria-describedby, and role attributes when using custom widgets
Use aria-live regions for asynchronous state notifications

title: Mouse-Only and Hover Traps
content: Interfaces requiring mouse hover to reveal actions or mouse coordinate gestures lock out keyboard-only users, switch device users, and voice control users. Interactions must never depend exclusively on pointer coordinate positioning or hover states.
recommended_alternatives: Display permanent action buttons or keyboard-accessible 'More Options' dropdown
Support standard Space/Enter and keyboard shortcut trigger
Provide persistent on-screen toolbar alternatives

title: Drag-and-Drop Accessible Alternatives
content: Drag-and-drop interactions in web applications (such as Kanban boards, file uploads, canvas reordering) create severe barriers. When an agent proposes dragging elements, it must confirm an accessible single-pointer or keyboard mechanism exists.
recommended_alternatives: Standard file upload button triggering system file browser dialog
Keyboard shortcut (e.g. Space to grab, Arrow keys to move, Space to drop)
Dedicated action buttons: 'Move Up', 'Move Down', 'Move to Top'

title: Icon-Only Buttons and Controls
content: Buttons with icons but no visible or programmatic text label cannot be announced by screen readers and are ambiguous to speech recognition users. Speech users cannot say 'Click Edit' if the button only contains a pencil glyph with no accessible name.
recommended_alternatives: Add aria-label='Edit Assignment' or aria-label='Delete Item' to the button
Include visible text adjacent to or inside the button element
Ensure tooltip or accessible text matches speech commands

title: Accessible Names on Interactive Controls
content: Every interactive control must have an accessible name that matches or contains the visual label. Mismatched or absent accessible names cause assistive tech users to struggle to identify the button's purpose.
recommended_alternatives: Provide descriptive text such as 'Submit DBMS Assignment' rather than 'Submit'
Match visible button text to the programmatic accessible name
Include svg <title> element inside vector icon buttons

title: Form Accessibility and Error Recovery
content: When users make input errors in forms, the error must be identified and described to the user in text, and suggestions for correction should be provided. Inaccessible form validation traps users who cannot see visual color changes.
recommended_alternatives: Use aria-invalid='true' and link error message with aria-describedby
Provide visible error summary at top of form with direct jump links to fields
Retain entered data across validation passes

title: Focus Management in Dynamic Interfaces
content: If content is modified dynamically (e.g. single-page app navigation, opening dialogs, deleting list items), keyboard focus must be moved logically. Losing focus to document body disorients keyboard and screen reader users.
recommended_alternatives: Trap keyboard focus inside active modal dialogs (Inert background)
When deleting an item, move focus to the next item or parent container
On SPA view transition, move focus to the primary <h1> heading

title: Error Prevention for Destructive Actions
content: For web pages that cause legal commitments, financial transactions, or modify/delete user data in storage systems, the user must be able to reverse the action, check the data for errors, or confirm the submission before finalizing.
recommended_alternatives: Require an explicit confirmation modal with clear impact explanation
Provide a review and edit screen before final irrevocable submission
Offer an undo window or soft-delete retention period

title: Timing Adjustable and Timeout Warnings
content: For each time limit that is set by the content, the user can turn off, adjust, or extend the time limit before expiring. Sudden timeouts cause loss of work for users with cognitive or physical limitations.
recommended_alternatives: Alert users at least 2 minutes prior to session expiration
Provide single keystroke extension button (e.g. 'Press Space to extend session')
Automatically auto-save form drafts to local storage

title: Contrast (Minimum) and Visual Clarity
content: The visual presentation of text and images of text must have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 (or 3:1 for large text). Low contrast buttons or subtle gray-on-white text are unreadable for people with low vision or color blindness.
recommended_alternatives: Ensure primary body text meets at least 4.5:1 contrast against background
Provide dark mode or high-contrast theme toggle
Do not convey information through color alone
